event.memo:
**Verdict: valid online product trading fraud (non-delivery) — evidence set complete and analyzable.**

- Victim paid AED 12,500 for an electronics bundle to a **personal** beneficiary account dictated over WhatsApp; goods never delivered, seller ghosted, page deleted.
- Evidence on file: 3 chat screenshots, transfer confirmation, bank statement.
- Priorities: reconcile chat ↔ receipt ↔ statement; verify the seller identity (OSINT); run the beneficiary account and IBAN through complaint history.

**Key identifiers**
- Complainant: Ahmed Hassan, +971 50 771 2094, Dubai
- Storefront: Prime Gulf Electronics — @primegulf.electronics
- Seller phone: +971 55 302 8817
- Beneficiary: Mubarak Salem
- Account: 5660609
- IBAN: AE600340005660609
- Amount: AED 12,500 on 2026-08-24
- Complaint: #002, filed {{FILED_DATE}}

**Verdict: scripted online-purchase fraud with payment steering to a personal account — the payment trail is fully documented in the images.**

- 15 Aug: victim contacts the seller after an Instagram ad; bundle offered at AED 12,500 vs claimed retail 16,800+ (−26%).
- Viewing refused ("free zone, no visitors"); COD refused ("insurance rules"); bank transfer only.
- 21 Aug: payment instructions name a **personal** beneficiary, justified as "finance manager" with the corporate account "under maintenance".
- Seller volunteers an **alternative account** (Abdullah Mohammed) — a second collection route.
- 24 Aug: transfer confirmed; fake order ref PG-1180; customs and courier excuses; fake refund promise; blocked by 30 Aug; page deleted 31 Aug.
- Transfer confirmation (image 4, Example Bank): ref TRX-2026-0824-4821, AED 12,500, 24 Aug 2026, purpose "Purchase of electronic devices", status Successful.
- Techniques: discount lure, trust signals, inspection avoidance, payment-method steering, ghosting.

**Key identifiers**
- Seller phone: +971 55 302 8817
- Instagram: @primegulf.electronics
- Beneficiary: Mubarak Salem — 5660609 — AE600340005660609
- Alternative account: Abdullah Mohammed — 3456660 — AE750340003456660
- Transfer ref: TRX-2026-0824-4821
- Order ref: PG-1180
- Amount: AED 12,500 on 2026-08-24

**Verdict: three-way reconciliation complete — chat, transfer confirmation and statement match to the reference number. Confirmed loss AED 12,500.**

- Reference, amount, beneficiary, account and IBAN identical across all three sources.
- Victim profile: salary AED 14,200; routine card spend AED 96–520. The transfer is the single outlier (36% of available balance).
- Freeze/disclosure targets: account 5660609 (primary) and 3456660 (alternative offered in the chat).

report.narrative: Ahmed Hassan, a Dubai resident, saw an Instagram advertisement in early August 2026 from a page called Prime Gulf Electronics offering discounted electronics. On 15 August he messaged the seller on WhatsApp (+971 55 302 8817), who presented himself as a company sales representative and offered a bundle of an iPhone, a MacBook, AirPods and an iPad for AED 12,500. The seller refused an in-person viewing and cash on delivery, and on 21 August sent payment details for a personal account — Mubarak Salem, account 5660609, IBAN AE600340005660609 — explaining that the company account was under maintenance. He also offered a second account under the name Abdullah Mohammed. On 24 August Mr Hassan transferred AED 12,500 from his Example Bank account (reference TRX-2026-0824-4821) and sent the confirmation. The seller acknowledged receipt and gave an order number, then followed with customs and courier excuses. From 30 August messages went unanswered, the Instagram page and website were taken down, and no refund was made. Mr Hassan filed this report on {{FILED_LONG}} with three chat screenshots, the transfer confirmation and his bank statement.
